title: Live: David Pocock demands Labor ensures 'fair return' from AI data centres
description: Independent senator David Pocock says the government needs to ensure a "fair return" for investment in artificial intelligence data centres. Follow live.
content_snippet: Hello and welcome to today's federal politics live blog! It's great to have you join us here early this Tuesday morning. I'm Josh Boscaini joining you live from Parliament House in Canberra, here an…
author: Joshua Boscaini
full_text: Federal politics: Coalition 'indistinguishable' from One Nation, PM says — as it happened Anthony Albanese says the Coalition is at risk of becoming "indistinguishable" from One Nation after the opposition leader did not rule out a preference deal. Look back at the day's coverage below. Submit a comment or question Live updates New: Filters Choose what information you see below by using filters Tue 9 Jun 2026 at 5:08pm That's all for today! Thanks for sticking with us. We'll be back tomorrow for another day on the federal politics live blog. You can look back at today's developments below, or download the ABC News app and subscribe to our range of news alerts for the latest updates. LoadingKey Event Tue 9 Jun 2026 at 4:53pm Preference deal with One Nation 'premature': Bell Liberal frontbencher Angie Bell says it's "premature" to be talking about a preference deal with One Nation. The party's federal director, Tony Abbott, endorsed swapping preferences with One Nation while Opposition Leader Angus Taylor left the door open to working with the minor party. But Bell has urged people to remember the election is still two years away. "What we need to be doing is working together as a credible opposition to offer the Australian people an alternative," she tells Afternoon Briefing. "I think it's premature for anybody to be talking about preference flows. "Because it's all hypotheticals at the moment. If our primary vote increases and we're able to get it up to the high 30s, early 40s, then we'll be in a different position in 18 months' time moving into an election. "So right now, I think polls come and go and we need to be focused on what we're doing as a Coalition to make sure we can get rid of this godawful Labor government." Tue 9 Jun 2026 at 4:33pm 'Ludicrous': Independent pushes back on claim three-day NDIS inquiry was long enough A three-day inquiry is currently underway into the government's proposed overhaul of the National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS). Labor frontbencher Murray Watt has dismissed concerns from advocates and stakeholders that it is too tight of a turnaround. "In terms of parliamentary inquiries, that's a pretty reasonable length of time. You don't have a lot of inquiries that go for a longer period of time," he says, arguing the issue has already been debated in the community. Independent MP Monique Ryan, who appeared on Afternoon Briefing after Watt, had a different view. "That's a ludicrous claim," she says. "The ethos of the NDIS was nothing about us without us. And that's exactly what the government has done. They have rammed through legislation without giving the disability community a chance to have appropriate input into the changes that they're facing," she says. Ryan says there is "absolutely no doubt" the scheme in its current form is unsustainable. But it doesn't mean concerns she has with the legislation, especially around the powers for a minister to decide funding for a certain class of supports, aren't valid. Tue 9 Jun 2026 at 4:26pm Rise in support for One Nation a reminder to focus on delivering: Watt Earlier today, Trade Minister Don Farrell suggested Labor doesn't have anything to fear from One Nation. That's despite the minor party leapfrogging Labor in a number of recent opinion polls as the most popular political party. Environment Minister Murray Watt says One Nation's current highs is thanks to the collapse in support for the Coalition. "From a Labor perspective, you know, we don't take the situation for granted. We acknowledge there has been a small drop in the poll from us potentially to other parties, including One Nation," he tells Afternoon Briefing. "But it's a reminder to us that we need to remain really focused on the issue that concerns Australians more than anything else, which has cost of living pressures." Watt says Labor must remain focused on the issue of cost of living and delivering support. Asked about federal Liberal president Tony Abbott's endorsement of a Coalition preference deal with One Nation, Watt says the party is "putting up the white flag" to the minor party. He noted Labor did swap preferences with the Greens but "no-one is suggesting there is any prospect of the Greens party winning anywhere near the kind of seats that One Nation is potentially going to gain". Tue 9 Jun 2026 at 4:18pm Watt in talks with state counterparts about data centres' energy and water useage Labor frontbencher Murray Watt is the first guest on today's edition of Afternoon Briefing. He's asked about the recent boom in data centres in Australia and how a proposal is assessed under the government's overhaul of environment laws. Watt says if a project is likely to have an impact on nationally protected matters, such as threatened species or "water levels" then it would require a federal assessment process. "The second point is that we already have developed expectations of data centres, which we are now following through in work that we're doing with states and territories around managing the energy and water use of those data centres," he says. The environment minister says he's having discussions with his state and territory counterparts about "how we can also make sure that data centres are built in a way that don't end up depriving the country of the water that we desperately need." Tue 9 Jun 2026 at 3:45pm Foreign students should return home before further study: Hanson One Nation wants foreign students to return home before applying for further study in Australia. Pauline Hanson said the policy was aimed at clamping down on "course hopping" by stopping university drop outs from receiving bridging visas while they wait. The proposed policy would also remove the mechanism to appeal to the Australian Review Tribunal. "It's apparent that when it comes to some of these students, there's no intention to study and every intention of abusing the system to access economic benefits and high Australian wages," Hanson said. "The system is being scammed, and universities addicted to foreign student money are part of the problem. "Many of these people are occupying homes and accessing services that should be for Australians first." The government noted back in 2024 the number of international students staying in Australia on a second, or subsequent visa, had grown 150,000 in 2022-23. In response, it placed conditions to stop individuals from going from course to course unless there was genuine progression and removed the ability for people on visitor visas to apply for student visas onshore. Tue 9 Jun 2026 at 3:14pm Coalition 'indistinguishable' from One Nation: PM Prime Minister Anthony Albanese says the opposition is at risk of becoming "indistinguishable" from One Nation after the opposition leader did not rule out a preference deal. Angus Taylor left the door open to a deal with One Nation, two years out from an election, saying he'd work with anyone to get rid of the current government. Speaking in Bendigo, Albanese noted that under John Howard the Coalition put One Nation last. "The problem for Angus Taylor is that if he tried to out One Nation, One Nation, then they become indistinguishable and people more and more will go towards what they see as the real thing," he says.  "John Howard used to put One Nation last. That says something about how right-wing the Liberal One National Parties have become. Three right-wing parties, all with a very common agenda." Tue 9 Jun 2026 at 3:05pm Allan 'absolutely' the best person to lead Labor to Vic election: PM Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has backed Jacinta Allan, declaring she's "absolutely" the best person to lead Labor to the Victorian election. "The premier is doing a great job and the premier is a proud regional representative as well," he says. "So she absolutely is the best person to lead Victoria because Victoria needs a strong premier." Allan has been under pressure in recent days amid reports her leadership could be challenged and a slide in opinion polls. Allan, who also represents the seat of Bendigo East, is expected to face a tough fight against the Nationals' Andrew Lethlean. Lethlean contested the last federal election, achieving a 10 per cent swing against Labor. Albanese says he's known Allan "for a long time" and she has a "record of delivering". Asked why the Victorian premier did not attend the TAFE alongside the prime minister, Albanese said they were meeting up tomorrow at the memorial for Neale Daniher. "I spoke with the premier last night. She's undertaking her duties in Melbourne. We speak regularly," he says. Tue 9 Jun 2026 at 2:45pm Albanese is speaking now Speaking of Anthony Albanese, he's just stepped up for a press conference. He's in Bendigo today, alongside local MP Lisa Chesters and Andrew Giles visiting the local TAFE. Stick around, I'll have all the latest for you as it comes in. Tue 9 Jun 2026 at 2:29pm Apple's new child safety features partly inspired by Australia, Albanese says Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Apple chief Tim Cook have spoken today after the technology giant unveiled a new range of child safety features. Advanced parental controls, including the 'Ask to Browse' and Time Allowances features, were announced at Apple's annual conference in California today. In a statement, the prime minister said Cook called him to say the changes were "in part inspired by Australia's world-leading social media age ban". "As well as the continued research Apple is undertaking into the impact of social media on kids," he said. "I welcome this announcement, and I am proud of the world-leading work Australia is doing to fight for a safer online world for our children. "We have a long way to go and we knew it would not be easy." Albanese said Cook invited him to visit Apple next time he was in the US. "I plan to take up that offer so we can keep learning how to best protect our kids," he said. "Social media companies have a social responsibility, and we make no apology for holding them to account to help keep kids safe." Tue 9 Jun 2026 at 1:25pm Analysis: New leader, old problem for WA Liberals as Zempilas flirts with One Nation One from our friends over in the west: Basil Zempilas's flirtation with One Nation is a classic example of how the more things change in politics, the more they stay the same. Addressing a business breakfast yesterday, the opposition leader — unprompted — declared leaders needed to understand ignoring One Nation "would be to ignore the will of the people". He had an "open mind" about a relationship with the maybe not-so-minor party, which upon further probing was revealed to range from preference deals to forming a coalition government. One Nation was not a threat, he insisted, but "an opportunity" to unseat Labor. "If people's frustration in Western Australia is so elevated that they are in a mood for change, as the leader of the Liberal-National alliance … I would be derelict in my duty not to look at all options to help bring that about," Zempilas added. Continue reading at the link below. Tue 9 Jun 2026 at 12:36pm The most contentious parts of the NDIS bill being scrutinised by the Senate Senators will today begin presiding over three days of hearings into legislation paving the way for the Albanese government to make the biggest cuts to the National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS). Australians were given just more than a fortnight to make submissions on the highly technical 113-page bill, which is accompanied by nearly 300 pages of explanatory notes and was referred to the Senate for an inquiry after being introduced to the lower house. The government has acknowledged the magnitude and speed of the changes, which have been slammed as "dangerous" by the disability community, but says they are needed to ensure the now-$50 billion NDIS remains sustainable for future generations. We've combed through the bill and hundreds of public submissions to unpack some of the most contentious parts of the proposed legislation and examine why they've been suggested. Tue 9 Jun 2026 at 11:48am How does Taylor hang on as leader? Rebuilding trust, he says Sussan Ley was only afforded nine months as leader of the opposition. As the Coalition continues to lag behind in the polls, how long does Angus Taylor give himself? The opposition leader goes back to idea of rebuilding trust. "I've said that a hundred times and I'll keep saying it. That's what we have to do," he says. "That's what we have to do and we're doing that by getting out and speaking to people ... ensuring we have the policies in place, policies for lower taxes, for cheaper energy, for more houses, for putting Australians first." Key Event Tue 9 Jun 2026 at 11:43am Taylor leaves door open to One Nation preference deal Opposition Leader Angus Taylor has left the door open to a preference deal with One Nation, declaring he'll work with anyone to get rid of Labor. "We'll work with others to get rid of a rotten Labor government," he says. "People are angry around Australia. I see it all the time. They've had enough of this rotten Labor government that's taking this country in the wrong direction." His remarks follow a report in the Australian Financial Review in which newly installed federal Liberal president Tony Abbott endorsed a preference swap with One Nation. Taylor was also asked about WA Liberal leader Basil Zempilas, who said he had an open mind to working with One Nation. "I want Australians' first preference but I know to get them I have to rebuild trust with those hard-working Australians who are angry because they have been dudded," he said. Tue 9 Jun 2026 at 11:35am Will the Coalition support the changes to the NDIS? Angus Taylor wouldn't be drawn on whether the opposition would ultimately support the government's sweeping changes to the National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS). "We're supporting an inquiry. We've got to have a sustainable outcome on the NDIS. I think every Australian wants to see a sustainable NDIS, and right now it's not," he says. "That's why we've supported an inquiry to make sure the legislation that comes to parliament for a vote in the end, in the Senate, is legislation that will deliver a sustainable outcome." A tight three-day inquiry has been scheduled for the Senate to examine the changes, amid concerns about tighter eligibility requirements and increased expectations on parents. The opposition had previously signalled it was willing to work with the Greens to extend the inquiry in exchange for support to extend a separate inquiry into the government's tax changes. Shadow NDIS Minister Melissa McIntosh says the opposition "fought hard" for the inquiry because the community was "hoodwinked" by the changes. Tue 9 Jun 2026 at 11:18am Angus Taylor talks up Coalition plan for housing as he visits Western Sydney Opposition Leader Angus Taylor is in Western Sydney today alongside Melissa McIntosh, talking to a local builder about housing supply. Taylor says the great Australian dream of owning a home is "disappearing in front of our eyes" and places the blame on the government and its recent budget. He argues the economy and the housing market is "frozen". Taylor points to the Coalition's plan to index income tax brackets to inflation and a proposed $5 billion housing infrastructure fund as a "better way" of handling issues in the market. Tue 9 Jun 2026 at 10:08am Analysis: Property and the budget ease pressure on the RBA as two banks cut fixed rates The older you get, the more frenetic the pace of life seems to become. No matter where you look, social, political and economic change appears to be in overdrive, and the long periods of stability we once enjoyed are becoming increasingly short-lived. Just look at the Reserve Bank. Last year, Australia looked to be on the verge of a slowdown, which was only to be expected after one of the fastest rate hike cycles in history, prompting the RBA to shave a couple of rate hikes off the top. But after it had cut for the third time, inflation again reared its ugly head and the RBA was forced into a sudden about-turn in 2026. Read the full analysis from chief business correspondent Ian Verrender in the link below. Tue 9 Jun 2026 at 9:19am Farrell says it's possible Australia could be slapped with a US tariff overlap Trade Minister Don Farrell says Australia rejects any suggestions that it should be linked with countries that were not doing enough to combat modern slavery and forced labour. It comes after the United States included Australia in a new 12.5 per cent tariff scheme due to come in from July, with allegations it was failing to address the importation of goods made with forced labour. Mr Farrell says he argued "strongly" that Australia should not face the import taxes with US counterpart Jamieson Greer last week. "We very strongly rejected that proposition," he says. "I've expressed to him how absolutely disappointed we are. "We should not be in this category." Mr Farrell says he does not exactly know whether the new 12.5 per cent import tax would overlap with the existing 10 per cent tariff currently imposed by the US on Australian goods. "There is a possibility that for a couple of days the tariffs might overlap, but they [the US] don't intend to enforce that overlap," Mr Farrell says. But he said the tariffs should be "zero" because Australia had a free trade agreement with the US. Tue 9 Jun 2026 at 9:03am Trade Minister says Labor does not have anything to fear from One Nation's rise in popularity Trade Minister Don Farrell says he doesn't think Labor has anything to fear from One Nation following another poll showing that more voters are interested in One Nation than any other party. Mr Farrell says populist parties "come and go" in Australian politics, recalling a 2017 opinion poll which suggested Nick Xenophon's SA Best party was more popular than Labor and the Liberals. "What happened at the election? He didn't win his seat," Mr Farrell says. "Populist parties in this country come and go, they rise and they fall. I don't think Labor has anything to fear from One Nation." "To the extent that anyone should be worried about One Nation, it should be the Coalition." Tue 9 Jun 2026 at 8:52am Additional 31,000 tonnes of fertiliser, 50 million litres of diesel secured: Farrell Trade Minister Don Farrell says the government has secured 31,000 tonnes of fertiliser and 50 million litres of diesel. The trade minister is back, fresh from a trip to Paris for the OECD Ministerial Council Meeting. Agriculture Minister Julie Collins says about 1.7 million tonnes of urea has arrived in Australia since the start of the Middle East war. "This is really important for our farmers provides them with some certainty in uncertain times and allows them to get on with their day jobs," Collins says.
